p: Nottingham's old centre is a maze of narrow lanes, and Bottle Lane is one of the little ones that links the bustle around the Old Market Square with the quieter streets towards the Lace Market. It's a reminder that this city was trading, brewing and partying long before bowling was invented. Finding a set of lanes tucked away down here is all part of the fun.

The city has a famous outlaw, and you won't be able to move for Robin Hood references. The statue near the castle is the classic photo stop, and it's an easy walk from here. Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem, built into the rock below the castle and one of the pubs that likes to claim the title of England's oldest, is also within reach if you fancy a pint with a bit of history before your game.

For your bowling night itself, a bit of planning goes a long way. If you're with a group, book a time that lets everyone arrive without rushing, because the first frame always goes better when nobody's out of breath. Sort the teams fairly, set a small prize for the winner, and maybe a silly one for the lowest score too. The person in last place is usually having the best time anyway.

Nottingham is a big student city, so weekday evenings can be just as lively as weekends during term time. If you prefer things a little quieter, an earlier slot tends to suit families of grown-ups and anyone who wants to chat rather than shout.
